docs.tests.node: This section is the catalog CHECKING ITSELF, rung by rung. Open a story and its checks run right away — opening the page is the request. Each step ticks past in the Interactions panel below the canvas (or behind the drawer button on a phone), and a red step names the claim that broke, not just the story.

The steps make the one measurement no headless layer can: they read pixels off a real WebGL canvas. "The plan says draw a square" and "a square is on the glass" have been different statements in this project before.
Automation opens the same stories and asserts on the same steps — one body, two consumers, no second copy to keep in step.
docs.tests.node.growth: The phone-reload case, replayed on demand. A page still laying itself out measures a scene at next to nothing; the renderer starts asynchronously; the real size arrives inside that start window — and a renderer that has not started cannot take a resize. The step builds a second scene of its own in a two-pixel box, grows the box in the same breath, waits the scene out and reads the glass: the card must be there at FULL size. Before the fix this was the canvas that came up empty on a phone until any toggle nudged it.
docs.tests.node.lifecycle: The first rung, and the one the rest stand on: a node is there, it goes, it comes back. The scene is fed a tree without the card and then one with it again — a new tree is new DATA, not a new showcase, so the canvas underneath never changes and no second WebGL context is spent. The last step runs twenty rounds and compares the first pixel to the final one: a renderer that ACCUMULATES looks right on frame one and wrong on frame twenty.
docs.tests.bounded: The second rung: the box. Bounded is the one atom whose whole lesson is invisible — it declares room and paints nothing — so every claim here is made through the debug outline, the same way the Atoms/Bounded shelf shows it.

The measurements are whole-glass, not point probes: an outline is a stroke a couple of device pixels wide, and a check that samples points either misses it or has to know where the stroke runs. The steps read the full buffer and answer with a count of inked pixels and their bounding box — a size claim is a claim about that box.
docs.tests.bounded.outline: Four claims on one canvas: the outline is the ONLY ink (the middle of the box still reads as desk — Bounded has no fill); a wider rect is a wider outline and no taller; square, circle, star and a hand-written path each leave a different pattern on the glass; and a node without Bounded leaves it bare — zero pixels, not merely fewer.
docs.tests.surfaced: The third rung: the paint. The rung below proves the box is real and invisible; this one is about the atom that finally draws, and about the seam neither rung below can reach — the AREA a surface is painted onto is not always the box a reader assumes.

The debug outline stays OFF here, unlike the Bounded rung: the steps measure what the SURFACE put down, and a hairline from another layer sits in the same buffer and would be counted as paint. Sizes are checked against arithmetic rather than a stored number — one unit is worth so many pixels at this etalon, so "the fill is 1.6 units wide" is exact on any screen.
docs.tests.surfaced.paint: Eight claims on one canvas. The fill covers exactly the box that was declared; a box without the atom and the atom without an area both leave the glass bare; re-registering the record repaints the node and moves no box; a record with no layers still draws its rim, in its own colour; a thicker rim inks more and a dashed one inks less, because width and dash are absolute lengths rather than a picture stretched to fit; plate, bare and zone are three different pictures; the paint may reach PAST the box (an outside-aligned border) or fall SHORT of it (a contained picture); and a desk with no box of its own takes its area from what it holds, shrinking when a child is taken away.
docs.tests.surfaced.area: Four claims about the OTHER area. `Surfaced` accepts a box or the extent of what a node holds, and this page takes the second branch apart: a container holding nothing paints nothing, and it is not a latch — one box brings the area back; children that carry no boxes reserve nothing, so plenty of content is still no area; a node with a box of its own paints THAT, even when it is smaller than what it holds, because the derived area is the fallback and not the sum; and the same two boxes in a row and in a free layout paint different areas, because the layout is what decided where they went.
docs.tests.surfaced.openwork: Five claims about a shape with no inside. One place is not a contour and paints nothing at any width; a solid line is walked out and back, so it has no free end and a round cap changes the picture not at all; cut it into dashes and the cap matters at once, because every dash has two ends of its own; an arrow is one path whose ends are set apart — a second head is more ink, the near end costs exactly what the far one does, and neither reaches past the run that was asked for; and the same walk under the stock `ink` and `trail` comes out solid or dashed, because the pattern belongs to the record.
